decisive_join: Turn the selective-label diagnosis into a bounded, lawful, role-relevant audit protocol that makes some missing outcomes observable without treating every rejection as an error or exploration as automatic entitlement.

findings.claim: Selective labels establish the structural missing-outcome problem: validation among selected people cannot observe the full rejected population.
limits: The direction and magnitude of error remain deployment-specific.

findings.claim: Bounded, pre-registered exploration provides one empirically supported route to making some otherwise missing candidate outcomes observable.
limits: The intervention does not mandate a universal rate and must still satisfy role relevance, accessibility, law, ethics, and equal treatment.

findings.claim: Shared-vendor correlation makes repeated application an unreliable assumption of independent market correction in the studied ecology.
limits: Recommendations are not identical final employer decisions and the finding does not generalize to every vendor or market.

findings.claim: The two-stage false-negative audit protocol is a normative research design, not adopted policy, proof that every rejection was wrong, or an entitlement to employment.
limits: Its denominators, randomization, candidate labor, accommodations, privacy, opportunity equalization, and outcome horizon require separate deployment authority.

observations.notes: Workplace outcomes are generally observed only after historical selection, leaving rejected candidates without comparable labels.
observations.subject: Historical selection policy

observations.notes: A hiring study demonstrates that pre-specified exploration can reveal candidates an exploitative policy would not select and can change measured quality and diversity.
observations.subject: Hiring exploration intervention

observations.notes: One shared-vendor ecology produced correlated recommendations and repeated rejection concentration above an independence baseline.
observations.subject: Shared screening vendor

observations.notes: NIST supplies voluntary Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage actions but does not create an employment-law safe harbor or a complete false-negative method.
observations.subject: AI risk management

observations.notes: Federal and NYC group-impact audits do not by themselves estimate the counterfactual success of rejected individuals.
observations.subject: Selection-rate audit
observations.value: group denominator, not individual false-negative rate

observations.notes: No source supplies a universal false-negative rate or proves that a rich-review pass, later success, or repeated rejection establishes the original counterfactual outcome.
observations.subject: All rejected candidates

selection_rule: Use selective-label, hiring-exploration, monoculture, NIST, and vendor-claim evidence to distinguish observed mechanisms, one empirical intervention, voluntary risk management, shared-vendor correlation, and the still-normative audit design.

prohibited_inferences: every rejected candidate was a false negative
a simulation pass proves job success
group bias audit equals individual false-negative audit
randomization cures unequal opportunity or measurement drift
one vendor ecology proves universal monoculture

title: False-negative observability, exploration, and shared-vendor correction
